Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation
Award
1.

By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the claim petition filed by the
petitioners under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of compensation.

2.  The petitioner has filed the present claim petition U/s 166/140 M.V Act, seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 25,00,000/- alongwith interest @ 24% p.a. from the date of filing of the present claim petition till its realization, for the permanent disability suffered by her in Motor Vehicular Accident which occurred on 28.08.2019 at about 11:15 am near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road, Narela, Delhi,
involving vehicle i.e. Motorcycle bearing registration no. HR10Y-6178 (offending vehicle) which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner.
3.

The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 28.08.2019, the petitioner/injured after MACP No. 193/20; FIR No.
389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 completing her daily work and bank work pertaining to bank account of her children, was going back to her home by riding her Honda Activa Scooty bearing registration no. DL11-SJ-3681.

At about 11:15 AM, when she reached near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road, Narela, Delhi, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against the aforesaid scooty of petitioner with a great force, as a result of which, she fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and permanent disablement.
Thereafter, she was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, where she was medically examined vide MLC No. 4496 dated 28.08.2019.

It is categorically averred that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR10Y-6178 being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein).
A case U/s 279/337 IPC was registered vide FIR No. 389/19 at PS. Narela with regard to the said accident.
The offending vehicle was found to be owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 as on the date of accident in question.

4. In their joint written statement, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner have claimed that offending vehicle was insured with respondent no. 3 at the time of accident and as such, insurance company is liable to pay compensation, if any to the petitioner.
On merits, they have denied the averments made in the claim petition and have prayed for its dismissal.
MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 5.
In its written statement, the respondent no. 3/insurance company claimed that raised preliminary objection that offending vehicle has been planted in the present case.
However, it has admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with it at the time of accident.
On merits, it has denied the averments made in DAR/claim petition and prayed for its dismissal.

2 6.

From the pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed vide order dated 07.04.2021:-
1.

Whether the injured Ms. Vandna suffered injuries in road traffic accident on 28.08.2019 at about 11:15 AM near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road, Narela,
Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS. Narela due to rashness and negligence on the part of the driver Sh. Mukul who was driving the vehicle bearing registration no.
HR10Y-6178, owned by Sh. Anuj Kumar Bhutani and insured with United India Insurance Co. Ltd?
OPP 2.
Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation if so to what amount and from whom?

OPP.
3.
Relief.
7. To substantiate her claim, the petitioner has examined only one witness i.e. herself as PW1 and her evidence was closed vide order dated 31.10.2022.
MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 8.

In defence, no evidence has been adduced by any of the respondents and their opportunity to lead respondent's evidence was closed vide order dated 01.02.2023.
9.
I have heard Ld. Counsel for the parties at length and perused the record including the pleadings and documents.
I have given thoughtful consideration to the same.

The issue wise determination is as under:-
10.
The onus to prove, the aforesaid issue was placed on the petitioner.

To prove the said issue,
petitioner/injured examined herself as PW1 by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A).
In her evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW1/A), injured/petitioner has deposed on the lines of averments made in the claim petition.

She has relied upon the following documents:-

record 4.

DAR Ex. PW1/5(colly)
5. Original Disability Certificate Ex. PW1/6 6. Estimate given by the doctor for Ex. PW1/7  future treatment 7. Photographs of her shop Ex. PW1/8  MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/

3 11. PW1 (injured herself) in her testimony by way of affidavit of chief-examination (Ex. PW1/A)
deposed that on 28.08.2019, after completing her daily work and bank work pertaining to account of her children, she was going back to her home by riding her Honda Activa Scooty bearing registration no. DL11-SJ-3681.

She further deposed that at about 11:15 AM, when she reached near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road, Narela, Delhi, offending vehicle which was being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit against her scooty with a great force, as a result of which, she fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

She further deposed that after the accident, she was taken to SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi,
where she was medically examined vide MLC No. 4496 dated 28.08.2019.

She categorically deposed that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing registration no. HR10Y-6178 being driven by its driver/respondent no. 1.

She further deposed that a case U/s 279/338 IPC was registered at P.S. Narela vide FIR No. 389/19 against the respondent no. 1.
12.
The aforesaid witness (PW1) was duly cross examined by the Ld. Counsel for the insurance company on the point of issue under consideration.
During her cross examination on behalf of insurance company, she admitted that at the time of accident, she was driving scooty.
She further admitted that she was not having DL at the time of accident and a kalandra u/s. 3/181 M.V. Act was booked against her for want of driving licence.
She MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 denied the suggestion that she was not working and earning anything at the time of accident.

Counsel for the petitioner has heavily relied upon the criminal case record [(which is part of DAR Ex. PW1/5 (colly.)] in order to bring home his point that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the alleged offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

He further argued that respondent no. 1 Sh. Mukul S/o Sh. Yashpal was also chargesheeted by the police for offences u/s. 279/338 IPC, which clearly establishes that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the alleged offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
14.

Per contra, Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/insurance company has raised arguments to seek exoneration of their liability despite admission of a valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

It has been contended that the petitioner was driving her scooty without valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and has prayed for deduction on account of contributory negligence.
15. The facts of the case, arguments of the Ld. Counsels, evidence, material on record and duly verified documents of the DAR have been carefully examined and scrutinized.

Respondent no. 1 namely Sh. Mukul S/o Sh. Yashpal (respondent no.1) has been charge sheeted for offences punishable U/s 279/338 IPC by the investigating agency after arriving at the MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle.
Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
4 16.

It is evident from the testimony of PW1 that the insurance company could not impeach her testimony through litmus test of cross- examination and said witness is found to have successfully withstood the test of cross-examination.
Even otherwise, PW1 herself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason or motive as to why she would depose falsely about the accident.
Moreover, FIR No.389/19 (which is part of DAR) is shown to have been registered on the statement of petitioner herself.
The contents of said FIR would show that the petitioner has disclosed therein the same sequence of facts leading to the accident as deposed by her as PW1 in her evidence.
Hence, there is no possibility of any false implication of driver of offending vehicle or false involvement of the said vehicle in this case.

17. It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle, was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

There is nothing on record to show that the injured/petitioner has any enmity MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.
Reliance placed on Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Co. Ltd.

18. Apart from above, copy of MLC (which is part of DAR) of injured prepared at SRHC Hospital,
Narela, Delhi shows that she was taken to said hospital with alleged history of RTA on 28.08.2019 at 12:12 PM.

On her local examination, she was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein and the nature of injuries sustained by her was opined as 'grievous' and later examined by the Competent Medical Board to assess the impact of the injury to have caused permanent disability to the extent of 51% in relation to her left lower limb.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in a motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to these documents from the side of respondents including insurance company.

19. Now, considering the contention of the insurance company as regards alleged contributory negligence, on the part of the injured herself as she was hit by the offending vehicle when she was going on a two wheeler/scooty and it is admitted by the petitioner in her evidence that she was not having any driving licence at the relevant time.

The law in this regard is well settled that the mere fact of absence of a driving licence by a victim driver shall not in itself imply that the vehicle was being driven in a rash and MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 negligent manner unless there is any rash and negligent driving proved on the victim's part.

Pronouncement by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal No. 3321/2008 titled Sudhir Kumar Rana V. Surinder Singh & Ors. and Civil Appeal No. 22966/2017 titled "Dinesh Kumar. J @
Dinesh J V. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., is relevant in this regard, wherein it has been held:

Dinesh Kumar. J @
Dinesh J V. National Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " Para9.
If a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.
The same, by itself, in our opinion may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently.

It is one thing to say that the appellant was Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
5 not possessing any licence but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two- wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having licence, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence....
"Para10.
The matter might have been different if by reason of his rash and negligent driving, the accident had taken place.
In view of the above position, we are of the view that the deduction of forty percent which was made on the ground of contributory negligence is without any basis.
Accordingly, we direct that the appellant shall be entitled to an additional amount of Rs. 4.60 lakhs which was wrongly disallowed.

20. There is nothing on record to show that the scooty was being driven by the injured/petitioner at an extraordinary high speed or rashly or that ordinary caution of a driver could have averted the accident.
None of the respondents have either been able to lead evidence on this aspect or breach the case of the petitioner to show any contributory negligence on the part of the injured/petitioner.

The facts of this case reveals that the accident took place when the offending vehicle which is a motorcycle being driven by MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 respondent no. 1, came at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty of the injured at point A as per the site plan.

Further, the mechanical inspection report which form part of DAR in respect of offending vehicle, shows damage on its front side, whereas, the mechanical inspection report of the scooty of the injured shows damage on its middle portion as also damage to the extent that its engine did not start, as an impact of the accident.
The extent of damage of the vehicle of the injured itself points to the reckless collision by the offending motorcycle, at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner.
There is no material, either during investigation or during trial that may show that the road accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the injured victim.
Merely because petitioner/injured was not holding DL at the time of accident

,
would not be sufficient to infer that there was any contributory negligence on her part or that any amount from compensation entitled towards her needs any deduction on this account.
Hence, the contention raised on behalf of insurance company in this regard, is hereby rejected.

21. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove his case on the basis of pre-ponderence of probabilities, that she sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 28.08.2019 at about 11:15 am near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road, Narela, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.

MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 22. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

23. It has been duly proved that the injured/petitioner Smt. Vandna sustained grievous injury in the road traffic accident occurred on 28.08.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent no.
Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
6 1/driver.

Consequent upon the injuries and permanent disability, the injured/petitioner suffered both physical and internal injuries, pain & suffering, incurred medical expenses, remained incapacitated to resume work immediately and therefore, suffered both personally and monetarily.
Accordingly, petitioner is entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

24. The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in injury cases has been laid down by Hon'ble Delhi High Court, in III (2007), ACC 676 titled as Oriental Insurance Co,.
Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors that: -
" The possession of one's own body is the first and most valuable all human rights and while awarding compensation for bodily injuries this primary element is to be kept in mind.

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co,.
Ltd., Vs. Vijay Kumar Mittal & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bodily injury is to be treated and varies on account of gravity of bodily injury.

Though it is impossible to equate money with human suffering, agony and personal deprivation, the Court and Tribunal should make an honest and serious attempt to award damages so far as money can MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19;
PS.
Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 compensate the loss.
Regard must be given to the gravity and degree of deprivation as well as the degree of awareness of the deprivation.
Damages awarded in personal injury cases must be substantial and not token damages".

25. It has been further held by the Hon'ble High Court that:
"the general principle which should govern the assessment of damages in persons injury cases is that the Court should award to injured persons such a sum as will put him in the same position as he would have been in the same position as he would have been in if he had not sustained injuries".
26.

The Hon'ble Apex Court pleased to consider the legal position for grant of reasonable and fair compensation and has laid down the binding guidelines that " the compensation should be just and is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly or a pittance".
Reliance is placed on 2012 (8) SLT 676 titled K. Suresh Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd.

sentences.text:
The golden principles for assessment of adequate compensation to victims of road accident have been appreciated by the full bench of Hon'ble Apex Court in 2017 (13) SCALE 12 : 2017 XI AD (SC) 113 titled National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors., wherein it has been held:-
"

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: .....The Tribunal and the Courts have to bear in mind that the basic principle lies in pragmatic computation which is in proximity to reality.
It is a well expected norm that money can not substitute a life lost but an effort has to be made for grant of just compensation having uniformity of approach.
There has to be a balance between the two extremes, that is, a windfall and the pittance, a bonanza and the modicum....."

MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
7 27.
Accordingly, the entitlement of injured/victim to just compensation is being assessed in the background of well settled parameters and guidelines as hereinbelow.
LOSS OF INCOME 28.
Petitioner has categorically deposed in her evidence by way of affidavit(Ex PW1/A) that she was working as a fish seller and earning an amount of Rs. 25,000/- per month at the time of accident.
She further deposed that due to the injuries suffered by her in the accident, she has suffered financial loss.
During her cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, she denied the suggestion that she was not working and earning anything at the time of accident.
She further denied the suggestion that she had not suffered loss of income due to the accident in question.

29. The Discharge Summary (Ex. PW1/3 colly) of Lok Nayak Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that she was admitted in the said hospital on 28.08.2019 and discharged on 31.08.2019.
As per the said record, the petitioner had sustained open grade IIIB B/B(L) leg.

Further, the Discharge Slip (which is also part of Ex. PW1/3 colly) of Lok Nayak Hospital, in respect of petitioner/injured, would reveal that she was again admitted in the said hospital on 27.11.2019 and discharged on 01.12.2019.
As per the said record, the petitioner had sustained fracture both bone leg with EHL weakness.
MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 30.

Apart from the aforesaid documents (Ex. PW1/3 colly) produced by petitioner, she has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which she had received the medical treatment.
It is apparent on record that petitioner had received treatment till 01.12.2019 as per discharge slip of Lok Nayak Hospital(which is part of Ex. PW1/3 colly).

Further PW1 has tendered certificate of assessment of permanent disability by the Medical Board of SRHC Hospital, which is a government hospital as Ex. PW1/6, wherein she has been found to have suffered 51% permanent disability in relation to her left lower limb.
The hospitalization record is proved for a period of 3-5 days on two occasions at a space of about three months.
Thereafter, she has been examined by the Competent Medical Board constituted at SRHC Hospital, Narela, Delhi, which had issued Disability Certificate dated 24.11.2021.

In the absence of any cogent evidence, it is reasonable to consider that the petitioner would have been precluded to resume her necessary activities of daily life for a period of 9 months which includes period of recovery also.

31. Apart from the bald statement made by the petitioner that she was earning Rs. 25,000/- per month, no tangible evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove any source of earnings of her at the time of accident in question.
PW1 has deposed that she was working as a fish seller at the relevant time and has affixed a photograph with a Signboard outside an empty shop.

The photograph (Ex. PW1/8) relied upon by the petitioner does not inspire the confidence of this Tribunal as the signboard does not find MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD:
19.09.2023 mention even location or address of the alleged shop and the picture does not show any inventory of the saleable goods to show that it was a shop.

There is material contradiction vide claim petition with that of her deposition claiming her occupation as a fish seller whereas while recording Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
8
her statement in terms of clause 29 of MCTAP, petitioner has disclosed her earning as Vegetable Vendor.
There is absence of any reliable material, to show the actual source of earning, if any of the petitioner and the place of work, from where she was working.
Petitioner has also failed to file any document in respect of ownership/rental/GST Voucher to prove her business.
32. The purpose of granting compensation is to ameliorate the sufferings of the victims of Motor Vehicle Accidents.
While deciding claim petition under M.V Act, the Claims Tribunal is guided by the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and realistic, pragmatic and liberal approach is appropriate.

It is pertinent to mention here that though, the working and earning of the petitioner has not been proved by her, however, it can not be denied that women being engaged in the same as compared to men, the fixing of notional income of a homemaker attains special significance.
There is nothing on record in respect of educational qualification of petitioner/injured.

Keeping in view that the petitioner, aged 33 years was an active person engaged in life activities and she was riding scooty bearing registration no. DL11-SJ-3681 at the time of accident, it shall be reasonable to assess the income of injured (disabled) as that of a skilled person.
MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 33.
It is now to be considered whether the earnings of the petitioner are to be assessed as at the place of accident or as at the place of residence of the petitioner.

It is established that accident in question took place on 28.08.2019 at about 11:15 am near Credence Global School, Safiyabad Road,
Narela, Delhi and FIR No. 389/19, u/s. 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Narela.

The petitioner has explained her presence at the spot of accident where she was hit while riding the scooty due to rash and negligent driving of offending motorcycle bearing no. HR10Y-6178 by the offending driver/respondent no. 1, causing her dangerous injuries and permanent disability.
As per her own deposition, petitioner was going after completion of her work at about 11:15 am for doing bank work pertaining to bank account of her children.
The location of the accident is at the border of Delhi adjacent to Haryana.

The petitioner is resident of Haryana and therefore, it is not out of place to infer that the presence of the petitioner at the place of accident does not point out towards here place of work at Delhi.
Even otherwise, it has been considered that the petitioner has failed to establish her income or location of work.
Therefore, it is reasonable to consider minimum wages as applicable to the place of residence which is in the State of Haryana during the period in question.
The prevalent minimum wages of a skilled person in the State of Haryana were Rs. 10,446.65p per month at the time of accident in question, which occurred on 28.08.2019.

Thus, a sum of Rs.
94,019.85p (10,446.65p x 9) which is rounded off to Rs. 94,000/-, is awarded in favour of petitioner and against the respondents under this head.
MACP No. 193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 LOSS OF FUTURE PROSPECT 34.
It is proved on record that at the time of accident, the petitioner was driving her scooty.

Although, she was challaned for not having driving licence at the time of accident but it has been considered while deciding issue no. 1 that no rashness was attributable by the victim in causing the Vandana vs Mukul And Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116179315/
9 accident in question.
Disability of the petitioner as 51% in relation to her left lower limb will definitely render lack of efficiency.
As per disability certificate (Ex. PW1/6) of petitioner, she has suffered 51% permanent physical impairment in relation to her left lower limb.
The petitioner has failed to summon any Medical Expert to examine the impact of the disability suffered by her which has been assessed vide permanent disability certificate Ex. PW1/6.

The opposing party/insurance company has not been granted opportunity to put its defence whether there has been any impact on the future earning of the petitioner due to the permanent disability suffered by her.
Future estimate (Ex. PW1/7) issued by the concerned doctor of Tulip Hospital has been relied upon claiming that the victim will require operation for her implant removal with bone grafting.
35. Law in this regard has been examined wherein the necessity of the examination of the Medical Expert for proving the disability certificate has been considered.

The court is guided by pronouncement of Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad passed in The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Amzad Khan & Ors, decided on 03.02.2016, pertaining to the case of victim having MACP No.
193/20; FIR No. 389/19; PS. Narela DOD: 19.09.2023 permanent disability, wherein Hon'ble Court has observed that the document is a public document and the contents of the same were not required to be proved in view of Section 77 of the Evidence Act and has been pleased to hold as under:-
".....In view of the provisions of Section 77 of the Evidence Act providing that the contents of public documents need not be proved by calling witness and the observations of the ApeX Court there was no necessity to prove the disability certificate by calling the Doctor

(Reliance has been placed by Allahabad High Court on observations of Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled Pt. Parmanand Katara Vs. Union of India and others, 1989(III)).

sentences.text: 36. The aforesaid ruling of the Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad is in the light of well settled legal position that emanates from Section 77 of Indian Evidence Act in regard to necessity of proving a public documents.
The statutory position has also been duly appreciated by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in respect of necessity of proving the disability certificate.

It has been observed by our own Hon'ble High Court in case titled " Suresh Chand Sharma Vs. Raju & Anr.", MAC APP. 373/2019,
decided on 27.07.2023 that an additional burden on the petitioner to prove the disability certificate can not be placed and in the absence of such proof, the claim of the petitioner /injured must not be restricted.
